runs.name: crates-final
runs.command: cargo test --no-fail-fast -p adage-learn -p adage-runtime -p adage-graph -p adage-tracks -p adage-pack -p adage-exec -p adage-hook

checks: Five prior sessions across distinct tasks produce a context and execution certificate using production defaults.
A fresh session with an intervening read selects the learned typed command; the approved native sandbox executes it successfully.
Missing and stale grants produce no fallback agent instruction; duplicate execution is withheld.
Related contexts and command selectors, failed-check recovery, negative outcomes, same-turn calls, task changes, exposure and independent session gates are covered.
CLI review decisions persist and all three harness replays remain silent for unapproved execution-only candidates.
Execution abstentions retire agent-follow judgments because no instruction was delivered; receipts remain the source of execution outcomes.
limitations: Synthetic native fixture grants exist only in temporary test homes and do not approve any real repository.
The broad affected-crate run preceded the final advisory-fallback guard; the CLI and focused native/learner tests cover the final fixes.
Overlapping test runs are listed separately; do not sum them as unique coverage.
Five optional tests are ignored; earlier real upstream staged-suite results are recorded separately.
No paid calls were made for this integration validation. Native Linux/Windows and real-code action elimination remain open.
Synthetic single-route execution does not establish calibrated precision for heterogeneous histories and installed context alphabets.
